diagnosis_explanation: Your right leg needed to be amputated below the knee. It was not healing well. This was related to poor blood flow in your body. It also relates to blockages in the arteries of your neck. You also had bypasses done to help blood flow to your legs. You have high blood pressure. You also have small pouches in your colon. Your thyroid gland does not make enough thyroid hormone. Your kidneys are not working as well as they should. You had an abscess in your intestine that was drained.
medication_rationale:
Acetaminophen 325 mg daily:
This medicine helps with pain. It can also lower a fever. You may not notice much when you take this. It is meant to help prevent pain from worsening. Some people get an upset stomach. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you get a skin rash.

Albuterol 2 puffs every six hours as needed:
This medicine helps you breathe easier. It opens up the airways in your lungs. You may feel your heart beat faster. You might also feel a little shaky. This is common. Call your doctor if your breathing does not get better.

Vitamin C 500 mg one to two times daily:
This is a vitamin. It helps your body heal. You may not notice any change. It supports your body's natural healing process. This medicine has no common side effects. Call your doctor if you get stomach pain.

Aspirin 81 mg daily:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. This can help with blood flow. You may not feel this medicine working. It is taken to protect your heart and brain. Some people get an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you get black or tarry stools. Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.

Symbicort 1 puff every morning and 1 puff every evening:
This medicine helps you breathe better. It reduces swelling in your airways. You might feel your heart beat faster. You may also get shaky. This is common. Rinse your mouth after using it. Call your doctor if your breathing gets worse.

Tums as needed:
This medicine helps with heartburn. It reduces stomach acid. You will likely feel relief from heartburn. You may have constipation. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you get stomach cramps.

Calcium 600 mg daily:
This helps keep your bones strong. It also helps your body work right. You may not notice this medicine. It supports your body's functions. Some people get constipation. This is common. Call your doctor if you get kidney stones.

Plavix 75 mg daily:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. This is important for blood flow. You may not feel this medicine working. It protects against clots forming. You might bruise more easily. This is common. Call your doctor if you bleed for a long time. Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.

Clorazepate dipotassium 7.5 mg every six hours as needed:
This medicine helps you relax. It can reduce anxiety and muscle spasms. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common. Do not drive or use machines. Call your doctor if you feel confused. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Lexapro 10 mg daily every night at bedtime:
This medicine helps improve your mood. It can help with feelings of sadness. You may notice a change in your mood over time. Some people get an upset stomach. You may also have trouble sleeping. This is common. Call your doctor if you think about hurting yourself.

Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg one-half tablet daily:
This medicine helps your body get rid of salt and water. This can lower your blood pressure. You may urinate more often. You might feel dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor if you get muscle cramps. Call your doctor if you feel very weak.

Ibuprofen 200 mg three pills as needed:
This medicine helps with pain and swelling. It can also lower a fever. You may feel relief from pain. You might get an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you have black, tarry stools.

Imdur 30 mg daily:
This medicine helps relax your blood vessels. This improves blood flow to your heart. You may get a headache. This is common. Call your doctor if you get severe headaches. Call your doctor if you feel faint.

Levoxyl 112 mcg daily:
This medicine replaces a hormone your thyroid gland makes. It helps your body's energy levels. You may feel more energetic. You might have a faster heart rate. This is common. Call your doctor if you have chest pain. Call your doctor if you get tremors.

Ativan 0.5 mg one-half tablet every six hours as needed:
This medicine helps calm you. It can reduce anxiety and restlessness. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common. Do not drive or use machines. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Call your doctor if you feel confused.

Lopressor 50 mg one-half tablet twice daily:
This medicine helps lower your blood pressure. It makes your heart beat slower. You may feel tired or dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor if your heart beats too slow. Call your doctor if you feel short of breath.

Flagyl 500 mg every six hours:
This medicine fights certain types of germs. It is used to treat infections. You might get an upset stomach. You may also have a metallic taste. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash. Call your doctor if you have severe diarrhea.

Multivitamin daily:
This vitamin helps fill gaps in your diet. It supports your body's health. You will likely not notice any change. It provides needed nutrients. This medicine has no common side effects. Call your doctor if you get stomach pain.

Nitrostat 0.4 mg to take as directed:
This medicine opens up blood vessels. This helps blood flow to your heart. You may get a headache. This is common. This medicine is for chest pain. Call your doctor if chest pain is not relieved. Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.

Omeprazole 20 mg daily:
This medicine reduces stomach acid. It helps with heartburn or ulcers. You may not notice much effect right away. It helps your stomach heal. Some people get diarrhea. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain.

Oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg every four to six hours as needed for pain:
This medicine helps relieve moderate to severe pain. It is a strong pain reliever. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. You might feel constipated. This is common. Do not drive or use machines. Call your doctor if you stop breathing. Call your doctor if you are too drowsy to wake up.

Lyrica 25 mg daily every night at bedtime:
This medicine helps with nerve pain. It can also help with anxiety. You may feel dizzy or sleepy. You might gain weight. This is common. Do not drive or use machines. Call your doctor if you have problems breathing. Call your doctor if you have swelling in your legs or feet.

Zocor 40 mg one-half tablet daily every night at bedtime:
This medicine lowers your cholesterol. High cholesterol can harm your heart. You may not notice any direct feeling. It works over time to protect your heart. You might get muscle aches. This is common. Call your doctor if you have severe muscle pain. Call your doctor if your urine is dark.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and sore from your procedure.
- Rest is important for healing right now.
- Keep the wound area clean and dry.
- Do not apply anything to the wound unless told to.
- Your goal this week is to rest and follow all wound care.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 100.4 F.
- Call your doctor if the wound looks red or has pus.

**Week 2:**
- You might still feel some pain or discomfort.
- You can start moving around your home more.
- Keep your wound clean and dry as instructed.
- Do not lift anything heavy.
- Your goal this week is to increase your walking distance inside your home.
- Call your doctor if pain gets worse instead of better.
- Call your doctor if you see more swelling or redness.

**Week 3:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- You can do light activities around your home.
- Avoid strenuous exercise or heavy lifting.
- Continue to care for your wound as directed.
- Your goal this week is to walk for short periods outside.
- Call your doctor if you have shortness of breath or chest pain.
- Call your doctor if the wound shows signs of infection.

**Week 4:**
- Your comfort level should continue to improve.
- You can slowly add more normal activities back.
- Do not stress the amputation site.
- Keep the wound clean and protected.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little longer each day.
- Call your doctor if you have any new or worsening symptoms.
- Call your doctor if the wheezing in your lungs gets worse.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Keep your wound clean and follow all instructions.
- Slowly increase your activity as you feel able.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- You cannot breathe: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: This needs help right now.
- Loss of consciousness: You are not responding now.
- Signs of stroke: Face droops or arm weakness.
- Chest pain or pressure: Your heart needs help now.
- Seizure: You are shaking uncontrollably.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks or pus are present.
- Severe pain not helped by medicine: Your pain is too bad.
- Cannot keep any liquids down: You cannot stay hydrated.
- Sudden large swelling in your leg: This could be a blood clot.
- New confusion or acting strange: Your thinking is unclear.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain improving slowly: Your pain is getting better.
- Questions about your medicine: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Wound healing slower than expected: No signs of infection are seen.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while you heal.
- Nausea without vomiting: You feel sick but not throwing up.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are slowly getting more energy.
- Minor redness not spreading: The redness is not getting larger.
